# Definition types

A data file is a JSON array of definitions, or a single one. Each is an object whose `type` names one of these types; the page of each lists its fields.

| Type | What it is |
|------|------------|
| [`ability`](ability.md) | Something a character has and can use: a skill, a spell, a power, a gift (08 §3). |
| [`action`](action.md) | Something a character does over time: phases with durations, the channels it occupies and the windows it opens (03 §6). |
| [`ambience`](ambience.md) | How a condition looks: a tint, a dimming and particles that fall or drift (12 §6.4). |
| [`anim`](anim.md) | A short keyframed effect at a place, or along the way from one place to another, played by a `show` (12 §7.3). |
| [`area_kind`](area_kind.md) | What every area of a kind starts with: tags, variables, clock, priority (02 §8.3). |
| [`atmosphere`](atmosphere.md) | What fills open cells of a stratum: density, pressure and the speed of sound (02 §4.1). |
| [`attribute`](attribute.md) | A number with a base and a stack of modifiers. |
| [`block`](block.md) | What occupies a cell's volume (02 §5.4). |
| [`body_function`](body_function.md) | Something a body as a whole can do to some degree, from what its working parts contribute (06 §6.3). |
| [`body_part`](body_part.md) | A kind of body part: layers of material, what it supplies, where others attach (06 §6.1). |
| [`body_plan`](body_plan.md) | The parts a body starts with and how they are joined (06 §6.2). |
| [`calendar`](calendar.md) | A realm's calendar (09 §14.2): the names of the parts of its day, each from a time of day, and the length of its year with the names of its seasons. |
| [`channel`](channel.md) | Something an action needs exclusive use of: an arm, the voice, attention (03 §6.2). |
| [`color`](color.md) | A colour: its `rgb`, the word text uses for it and the terminal colour shown in its place (12 §4.3). |
| [`content_table`](content_table.md) | A content table (06 §9.3): what a cell, a shelf or a container is found to hold, as weighted entries of items, of other tables and of nothing, shared by every map and table that names it. |
| [`contest`](contest.md) | A comparison of two numbers with chance: their difference or log-ratio, scaled, with logistic noise of a given spread (07 §4.1). |
| [`control`](control.md) | Something the player can do, by a name a keymap gives to a key: interface effects to run (12 §9.2). |
| [`damage_type`](damage_type.md) | A kind of harm, with the resistance of anything that states none of its own (02 §12.2). |
| [`device`](device.md) | What an element becomes when it needs state of its own, or a machine standing alone: what it holds, its tags, modes, settings and stores, how fast and whether by itself it works recipes, and the know-how it provides (16 §4.2). |
| [`eoc`](eoc.md) | A rule: when an event happens, or when it is called, if a condition holds, do a list of effects (05 §9). |
| [`event`](event.md) | An event that a mod raises with `emit` and that rules listen for: its subjects, its fields, and whether it is a hook (05 §8.1). |
| [`event_signal`](event_signal.md) | An event that gives off a signal where it happens, with a strength worked out from the event (15 §3.2). |
| [`field`](field.md) | A per-cell value from 0 to 255 that evolves by rule: fire, smoke, water (02 §16). |
| [`field_reaction`](field_reaction.md) | What two fields do to each other, what a field does where it meets a tagged material, or how a field passes on damage that arrives in it (02 §16). |
| [`figure`](figure.md) | Rows of character art with named regions, drawn by the `figure` widget (12 §10.3). |
| [`fixture`](fixture.md) | A static prop standing in a cell (02 §5.4). |
| [`floor`](floor.md) | The surface at the base of a cell (02 §5.4). |
| [`function`](function.md) | A named, parameterised value that expressions call (05 §12). |
| [`goal`](goal.md) | A goal: how much a character wants it, what it is about, how it is pursued, and when it is over (09 §3.2). |
| [`ground`](ground.md) | What the ground of a tract is made of: strata, a surface, liquid, veins, pockets, caves and scattered things, as steps run in order for each tract (10 §5). |
| [`group`](group.md) | A body of people: its roles, who in it may order whom, and what it holds toward other groups from the start (15 §9.2). |
| [`interaction`](interaction.md) | Something a character can do to a thing: its reach, time, conditions and effects (16 §3.1). |
| [`item`](item.md) | A kind of item: what it is made of, how it is held and worn, what it holds and what it confers (06 §9.1). |
| [`keymap`](keymap.md) | For each context, the name each key has in it (12 §9.2). |
| [`know_how`](know_how.md) | Something someone may know how to do, held by a mind and asked for by recipes; what must be known first (16 §8.5). |
| [`lines`](lines.md) | A table of things to say, each a text with a condition and a weight; one that fits is picked when something is said (15 §11). |
| [`map`](map.md) | A place written as rows of characters, one layer for each storey, with a palette saying what each character stands for (10 §3). |
| [`material`](material.md) | What elements are made of: density, toughness and resistances (02 §5.4). |
| [`message_kind`](message_kind.md) | A kind of message said aloud: what it carries for the engine (a report, an order, or nothing), and how it is said (15 §11). |
| [`method`](method.md) | A method written on its own: a condition and the steps that pursue a goal, which become the character's actions one at a time (09 §4). |
| [`mind`](mind.md) | A mind: the goals a character may have, the weights that colour its choices, how often it thinks, and how it stands toward others (09 §3.1). |
| [`mission`](mission.md) | A template for objectives, started with parameters by `start_mission`: a bounty, a delivery, a job (13 §5.2). |
| [`movement`](movement.md) | A way of moving: where it takes its mover, how fast, and what it needs (06 §11). |
| [`overlay`](overlay.md) | Shading a map view draws over its cells where an expression over a cell holds (12 §6.2). |
| [`palette`](palette.md) | What each character of a map stands for, shared between maps (10 §3.2). |
| [`path_kind`](path_kind.md) | What a path is made of: how wide it is and the floor laid along it, with a strip of another floor along each side (10 §8.5). |
| [`plane`](plane.md) | An interaction layer: occupants that share no plane do not meet (02 §8.2). |
| [`pool`](pool.md) | A bounded quantity that fills, drains and regenerates. |
| [`posture`](posture.md) | How a body holds itself: what that makes of its height, its speed, how it is perceived and what it can use (06 §11.1). |
| [`preference`](preference.md) | A player's choice about display and input, kept outside saves and invisible to rules (12 §10.4). |
| [`projectile`](projectile.md) | A kind of projectile: a mass with a cross-section and a striking surface that flies as a body when something shoots (07 §11.1). |
| [`realm`](realm.md) | A world: its extent, wrap, storeys, strata, fill, clock rate and edges (02 §4.1). |
| [`reason`](reason.md) | A reason a mod gives for a refusal of its own: a sentence and the values it carries (14 §15). |
| [`recipe`](recipe.md) | What is used up, what is needed, how much work it takes and what it gives: crafting by hand, processing at a station, cooking, brewing and growing (16 §8). |
| [`region_kind`](region_kind.md) | The recipe for surveying a region: its tract definitions in patches, the sites it holds, the settlements it may hold and the paths that cross its edges (10 §8.1). |
| [`relation_kind`](relation_kind.md) | A kind of relation a mind holds toward a persona or a group: its range, default, fade, and the flags `opposes`, `sides_with`, `avoids`, `orders` and `intervenes` the engine reads (15 §9.1). |
| [`routine`](routine.md) | A routine (09 §10.2): the parts of a character's day, each beginning at a time of day, with the place it is meant to be by role (home, a site by definition or tag), what it is doing, and the goal it pursues there while loaded. |
| [`rule_group`](rule_group.md) | A set of rules that is switched on and off together (05 §9.6). |
| [`scenario`](scenario.md) | A game the player can start: its worlds, who the player is and where they begin, the rules in force, its objectives, how it ends and how it is saved (13 §3). |
| [`screen`](screen.md) | A screen of the interface: its variables, its layout tree and its keys (12 §10.1). |
| [`sense`](sense.md) | What an entity perceives signals of one kind with: its range, arc, threshold and how fast awareness builds and fades (15 §4). |
| [`setting`](setting.md) | A choice content offers players, read by rules with `setting(id)` and changed only by the `Setting` command (04 §10). |
| [`settlement`](settlement.md) | A town, a village or a camp: a pattern of streets, the lots between them filled by maps chosen by zone, and the sites every instance has (10 §8.4). |
| [`show`](show.md) | How an event appears when it is played back: changes to the picture, an animation, a log line, what to do if it was only heard (12 §7.3). |
| [`signal_kind`](signal_kind.md) | A kind of signal: light off a body, a sound, a scent. |
| [`site`](site.md) | A named place with identity: the map that stands there, its roles from the map's marks, and who works there (10 §11.1). |
| [`sky`](sky.md) | The light a stratum's sky gives by time of day, how it spreads under cover, and a backdrop (15 §3.3). |
| [`substance`](substance.md) | One stuff, whatever form it is in: what it tastes of, what it is as a spill, and what a dose of it does in a body by each route (16 §9.5). |
| [`template`](template.md) | What a kind of thing is made of: a body, stats, tags, rules, starting traits and items, and choices (06 §10). |
| [`theme`](theme.md) | Colours and styles by name, border characters, a font and the engine's marks (12 §4.3). |
| [`track`](track.md) | An accumulating counter with levels. |
| [`tract`](tract.md) | What kind of place a tract is: its ground, the maps that stand on it, the travel bands that cross it, its ruin and its glyph (10 §6). |
| [`trait`](trait.md) | Anything an entity has that changes what it is or can do: a feature, a mutation, a perk, a blessing, a curse, a drug, a stun, a stance (06 §5). |
| [`ui_part`](ui_part.md) | A widget put into a slot of a screen, in `order`, shown while its `if` holds (12 §10.6). |
| [`variable`](variable.md) | A declared variable: what it lives on, its type and its default (05 §6). |
| [`window_kind`](window_kind.md) | A kind of reaction window: how soon and whether it is noticed, and how far its offer reaches (03 §7.1). |

## Keys every definition carries

These keys are read by the loader itself, on any definition, before its type sees it (04 §5, §6). Any other key belongs to the type.

- `type`: The definition type: one of the types of this reference. Required.
- `id`: The definition's id. A bare name defines it in the namespace of the mod that wrote it; a qualified `namespace:name` in another namespace is allowed only with `patch` or `override`. Required.
- `//`: A comment. Ignored anywhere, at any depth.
- `abstract`: `true`: the definition exists only to be inherited from with `copy_from`. It is never instantiated, and need not give every required field. Not inherited.
- `if_mod`: A mod id, or a list of them: the definition is read only if every one is in the profile.
- `unless_mod`: A mod id, or a list of them: the definition is read only if none is in the profile.
- `obsolete`: `true`: the definition stays loadable so that saves that name it work, and is left out of generation, spawning and lists. Referring to it from a definition that is not obsolete is a warning. Not inherited.
- `copy_from`: The id of a definition of the same type: this one is that one's finished definition with this object applied as a change (04 §6.2). It may be defined later or in another mod.
- `patch`: `true`: changes the existing definition of this id in place, field by field (04 §6.3). Patches apply in load order; patching what does not exist is an error unless `optional` is set.
- `override`: `true`: replaces the existing definition of this id completely (04 §6.4). Earlier patches are discarded.
- `optional`: With `patch`: if there is nothing to patch, skip this object rather than report an error.
- `extend`: An object of field paths and values to append to a list or a set, or merge into a map: `{ "tags": ["x"] }` (04 §6.1).
- `delete`: An object of field paths and entries to remove from a list or a set, or keys to remove from a map: `{ "tags": ["y"] }`.
- `scale`: An object of field paths and factors to multiply numbers by: `{ "density": 1.2 }`. Applied once the final value is known, before `add`.
- `add`: An object of field paths and amounts to add to numbers, which may carry a unit: `{ "span": 2 }`.
